title: React Error Boundaries, Suspense and lazy() Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on what error boundaries catch and miss, class and react-error-boundary usage, Suspense loading states, lazy() code splitting, and designing error and loading UX.

chapters.title: Error Boundaries: The Mental Model
points: An error boundary is a component that catches errors thrown during rendering of its child tree and shows a fallback UI instead of unmounting the whole app
It catches errors in render, lifecycle methods and constructors of descendants; the error propagates up to the nearest boundary only
It does NOT catch event handler errors, async code (setTimeout, promises, fetch callbacks), SSR errors, or errors thrown in the boundary itself
Event handlers: use try/catch; async errors: catch and call setState(() => { throw err }) or use showBoundary to route into a boundary
With no boundary in the tree, an uncaught render error unmounts the entire React tree (blank screen)

chapters.title: Class Boundaries and react-error-boundary
points: Class boundary needs static getDerivedStateFromError(error) returning state like { hasError: true } to render the fallback
componentDidCatch(error, info) is for side effects such as logging; info.componentStack gives the component trace
There is no hooks equivalent for boundaries; function components cannot be boundaries, so use a class or a library
react-error-boundary: <ErrorBoundary FallbackComponent={Fallback} onError={log} onReset={fn}> wraps a subtree
Fallback receives { error, resetErrorBoundary }; resetKeys={[id]} auto-resets when a listed value changes
useErrorBoundary() returns showBoundary(err) to push event handler or async errors into the nearest boundary

chapters.title: Suspense for Loading States
points: <Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}> shows the fallback while any child below it is suspended (not ready to render)
A component suspends via lazy(), a Suspense-enabled data source (use(promise), framework data fetching, cache libraries); useEffect fetching does NOT trigger Suspense
Nearest ancestor Suspense wins; nesting boundaries gives granular fallbacks (page shell first, widgets load later)
Wrap updates in startTransition or useDeferredValue so already shown content stays visible instead of reverting to the fallback
Pair with an error boundary: Suspense handles pending, error boundary handles rejected; order is ErrorBoundary outside, Suspense inside

chapters.title: lazy() and Code Splitting
points: const Page = lazy(() => import('./Page')) defers loading the chunk until first render; the module must have a default export
A lazy component with no ancestor Suspense does not throw and has no fallback: React keeps what is on screen, which is blank on first render, until the chunk loads
Split at route level first, then at heavy components (charts, editors, modals) loaded on demand
Declare lazy() at module top level; declaring it inside a component creates a new type each render and resets state
Chunk load failure (offline, stale deploy) rejects the import; an error boundary with a retry button catches it
Named exports: lazy(() => import('./X').then(m => ({ default: m.X })))

chapters.title: Error and Loading UX Patterns
points: Place boundaries at multiple levels: app root for crashes, route level for page failures, widget level so one failure does not take down the page
Fallback must offer recovery: a clear message, a Retry button calling resetErrorBoundary, and navigation away; never show raw stack traces to users
Prefer skeletons that match the final layout over spinners to cut layout shift; delay spinners about 200ms to avoid flicker on fast loads
Log in onError / componentDidCatch to a monitoring service (e.g. Sentry) since production users never see the console
Common mistake: one global boundary only, so any widget error blanks the whole page; another is a Suspense fallback that is bigger or different from the content

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet
points: Boundary catches: render, lifecycle, constructors of children; misses: event handlers, async, SSR, itself
Class API: getDerivedStateFromError (set fallback state), componentDidCatch (log)
react-error-boundary: FallbackComponent, onError, onReset, resetKeys, useErrorBoundary().showBoundary
Suspense: fallback while child suspends; ErrorBoundary outside, Suspense inside; use startTransition to keep content
lazy(() => import('./X')): top level, default export, needs Suspense, split by route first, retry on chunk failure
